sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975. Languages of Irian Jaya: Checklist. Preliminary classification, language maps, wordlists (Pacific Linguistics B-31). Canberra: ANU. Appendix 'Comparative wordlists', note on orthography p.92.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: The comparative 40-item wordlists (Yafi included, forms visible via transnewguinea.org) use a unified orthography in which 'Stress and pitch are not indicated.' (p.92). Cannot bear on Yafi stress.

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. n.d. [last modified 2024-06-25]. East Pauwasi River. Newguineaworld (University of Zurich). Proto-East-Pauwasi-River phonology and 171 reconstructions with Zorop reflexes (Warlef after Lee 2005; Tokondo after Walton in Smits & Voorhoeve 1994), Emem (Lebold) and Karkar (Price).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No statement on stress or tone for Zorop or for Proto-East-Pauwasi. Wordlist-only data: the Zorop (Warlef, Lee 2005) column has 381 forms with vowel-length marks on 29 but no stress marks at all; Zorop (Tokondo) 154 forms, no stress marks; by contrast Emem (Lebold) and Karkar (Price) forms carry primary-stress marks (82, 72, 53 forms). The Sources section cites 'Price (1981) Karkar stress' for the sister language only.

sources.citation: Pawley, Andrew & Harald Hammarström. 2018. The Trans New Guinea family. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area: A Comprehensive Guide (The World of Linguistics 4), 21-195. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton. Sec. 2.3.2.4 'Pauwasi', pp. 73-74.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: No phonology content for Yafi. Documentation-status line only: 'Yafi [wfg] 230; wordlist: Galis 1956, Voorhoeve 1971, 1975'; 'The Pauwasi languages are scantily documented but Tebi and Yafi show a few possible reflexes of pTNG etyma' (Yafi nam '1SG', nim '1PL', yemar 'louse'). Confirms second-hand that the most extensive description of Yafi is a wordlist; sister language Karkar-Yuri has 'grammar sketch: Rigden no date'.

sources.citation: Hammarström, Harald. 2010. The status of the least documented language families in the world. Language Documentation & Conservation 4: 177-212.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent on stress. p.~198: Zorop [wfg] and Emem [enr] known only from wordlists (Voorhoeve 1971, 1975a:418-419; Whitehouse 2006 type-ups); Usher links them to Karkar-Yuri; family counted as documented only via Karkar-Yuri materials (Price 1987; Rigden n.d.).

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2007. Change Request 2007-229: [wfg] Yafi -> Zorop (submitted by Randy Lebold, SIL).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing linguistic; documents the March 2005 SIL rapid-appraisal survey, autonym Zorop, exonym Warlef (village name), and cites 'Report on the Zorop (Yafi) Language. draft' as the only source.

sources.citation: Whitehouse, Paul. 2006. The 'Lost' Paper: A Belated Conference Postscript. Mother Tongue (Journal of the Association for the Study of Language in Prehistory) XI: 262-274. [pp. 267-268 'A New Grouping in Central New Guinea?']
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No phonology content; long-range comparative etymologies (Kehu, Bulaka River-Trans Fly, expanded Pauwasi) reporting Usher's pers. comm. that Karkar-Yuri belongs to the Yafi-Emumu subgroup.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975. Central and Western Trans-New Guinea Phylum languages. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1 (Pacific Linguistics C-38), 345-460. Canberra: ANU. Sec. 2.6.2.2.13 'The Pauwasi Stock', pp.418-419.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent: 'The only published source of information is Voorhoeve 1971; the data on hand is restricted to word lists.' Gives only location and speaker numbers for Yafi (170 speakers).

sources.citation: TransNewGuinea.org, 'Zorop' language page (150 lexical items from Voorhoeve 1971 and Voorhoeve 1975).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Lexical forms only (jai, unduk, jalək, məndai..), no stress marks; confirms the only lexical sources are Voorhoeve 1971/1975.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1971. Miscellaneous notes on languages in West Irian, New Guinea. In T. Dutton et al., Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 14 (Pacific Linguistics A-28), 47-114. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing for Jafi/Yafi. Sec. 2.6 'The Pauwasi Phylum' (p.77): 'The only data on hand is the wordlists collected by Galis (1956b). These are sufficient for purposes of provisional classification, but do not allow conclusions about phonological and grammatical structure.' Appendix I gives an 80-item comparative Jafi wordlist (from Galis) with no stress marking. (The stress remarks on p.~75, 'The place of the accent is not fixed..', belong to sec. 2.5.3, a Senagi-family language, not Yafi.)

sources.citation: Badan Pengembangan dan Pembinaan Bahasa (Kemendikdasmen). n.d. Peta Bahasa: 'Bahasa Yafi', Provinsi Papua (idb 719). [Kampung Warlef = Dusun Tokondo, Abiu, Sungguar, Tainda; Distrik Senggi, Kabupaten Keerom; 'dituturkan oleh etnik Jorof'; dialectometry vs Tefanma and Molof 98.75%.]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)

sources.note: No phonology content: location, neighbouring languages (Yabanda E, Senggi W, Walsa N, Dubu S) and a dialectometry percentage only. Indicates Badan Bahasa collected its standard basic-vocabulary list in Warlef (underlying data unpublished).

sources.citation: Foley, William A. 2018. The languages of the Sepik-Ramu basin and environs. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area: A Comprehensive Guide, 197-432. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.

sources.citation: Lee, Sangkem. 2005. Draft Survey Report on the Zorop language of Papua, Indonesia. SIL International, Indonesia Branch (Papua survey team), unpublished draft ('to appear in SIL Electronic Survey Reports'; cited in ISO 639-3 CR 2007-229).

sources.note: The only post-1956 first-hand data on Zorop (March 2005 SIL rapid appraisal in Warlef village). Ask SIL Indonesia / SIL Language & Culture Archives (REAP) for the draft and wordlist.
